newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs close mostly lower, pork bellies higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs close mostly lower, pork bellies higher.

text.p: CME hog futures found late short covering but closed mostly lower on liquidation and new selling interest while pork bellies held gains sparked by a South Korean pork tender, traders said. Local long liquidation added to new selling to keep hog futures pressured despite late short covering. December led the setback on bear spreading, they said. Expectations that top cash hog prices will decline to the $52 per cwt level before stabilizing kept futures under pressure. Top prices Friday at Midwest interior markets for cash hogs ranged from $53.00 to $54.50 per cwt -- the latter paid in Iowa/southern Minnesota trade. Cash loin prices were expected to decline seasonally which likely will squeeze packer margins, sources said. South Korea's pork tender sparked only minimal support after rallying the market briefly Thursday, as the largest of the tenders was to meet that country's 1997 trade agreements under the Minimum Market Access import quotas, making it routine business and largely expected.
Sources said increased domestic demand for pork or lighter hog marketings are needed to turn pork prices around. (c) Reuters Limited 1996
